thread:
ops-bot: INCIDENT — High inference latency (p95) for hosted-api in us-west-2. Pager sent to oncall.
eli: got the page, I'm on it. pinging infra and perf. any customer-facing alerts triggered? :loudspeaker:
alice: customer-facing SLA page showed increased 5xx? I see error-rate flat but latency up — looks like tail only. p50 ~120ms, p95 jumped from 260ms -> 1.1s since ~2h ago.
ben: confirmed, good catch. correlated with a kernel upgrade event in the node pool around 2h ago (kube rolling upgrade job).
carla: linking trace for one slow request: https://traces.internal/r/abcd1234 — span shows big gap in `inference.decode` between token 12–32.
david: sharing perf counters from one affected host (sanitized):
```
perf stat -e context-switches,cpu-migrations,cs,migrations -p 1234
# 2:00:05 PM
context-switches: 12,345,678
cpu-migrations: 45,678
```
frank: also saw higher `softirq` and `sched_wakeup` latencies in `perf sched` output.
eli: hypothesis: kernel scheduler change increased scheduling latency for our inference threads under bursty workloads. need to validate with dmesg and upgrade ops.
ben: pulling node upgrade history now. kube-controller shows daemonset `node-upgrade` rolled kernel to 5.18.12 -> 5.19.1 around 03:04:12 UTC.
alice: impact scope: 12% of requests in prod in us-west-2 hit p95 > 1s over the last 30m. No increase in errors, so functionality intact but bad latency for customers streaming tokens.
carla: collecting perf samples across 3 nodes. adding stack traces and `perf top` snapshots. will drop them here when ready.
ops-bot: Incident channel escalated to SEV2. Runbook run: https://runbooks.internal/latency-regression
eli: mitigation options: 1) roll back kernel on affected nodepool (image rollback) 2) drain & reprovision nodes to previous AMI 3) roll traffic away from us-west-2 to standby region 4) temporary autoscale more inference workers to reduce scheduling pressure.
alice: we should avoid region failover unless necessary. prefer draining affected nodes to AMI with previous kernel + rolling restart of inference service.
ben: I can start a targeted drain of one node to verify latency drop (canary). starting drain on node ip-10-2-45-7 now.
carla: perf sample from node ip-10-2-45-7 pre-drain:
```
# perf record -F 99 -a -g -- sleep 60
# perf script | head
inference.decode  {  0.00 }  sys_sched_yield
inference.decode  {  0.00 }  __schedule
```
frank: that matches higher scheduler time. after drain, I'll capture a second sample.
eli: coordinating customer comms — notifying support to append temporary note: "Intermittent higher tail latency in us-west-2 for streaming responses; working on mitigation." @support-team please prepare.
alice: can we get trace span ids for 10 slow requests? I put a query in `traces` for p95 > 900ms; link: https://traces.internal/query?service=hosted-api&latency>900
ben: drain completed on canary node. immediate check — p95 on that canary pool dropped to 240ms within 3 minutes. looks promising :thumbsup:
carla: perf sample post-drain (same test) shows scheduling stall gone. attaching snippet:
```
# post-drain perf script
inference.decode { 0.00 } do_syscall_64
inference.decode { 0.00 } memcpy
```
david: confirmed: kernel version on drained node is still 5.18.12 (old), the other nodes are 5.19.1. can we roll the rest back to 5.18.12? need approvals for AMI reversion.
eli: action items list (in-thread tracking):
- [Eli] coordinate rollback plan and convo with infra for AMI reversion (started)
- [Ben] drain & canary nodes (done for 1 node)
- [Carla] collect full perf samples and upload artifacts (in progress)
- [David] gather k8s upgrade job logs and which batches rolled (in progress)
- [Frank] check kernel changelog for scheduler flags changed in 5.19.1 (investigating)
- [Alice] craft support note and customer advisory draft (in progress)

carla: uploaded perf tarball to the incident folder: https://artifacts.internal/incidents/1769001234/perf.tar.gz
ben: scaling additional workers in the pool by +20% to reduce queueing while we rollback — doing now.
ops-bot: NOTE — autoscale event triggered: scaled inference-pool-usw2 from 120 -> 144 pods
eli: next — need oncall handoff at +90m. @frank can you take next 2h? I'll stay as incident lead for the RCA.
frank: I can take the handoff. please paste current hypothesis & timeline before I fully take over.
eli: timeline (building):
T-2h: automated node kernel upgrade rolled 5.19.1 to 60% of nodes
T-1h50m: first p95 uptick detected by metric rule
T-1h30m: alerts page + oncall pager
T-1h10m: canary drain started
T-1h05m: canary p95 dropped to normal
T-50m: scaling +20% completed
T-40m: perf artifacts uploaded
T-30m: mitigation plan: roll back full nodepool in batches (waiting infra approval)

frank: got it. I'll continue monitoring, collect more traces, and start the rollback play once infra signs off.
alice: support note v1:
"We're investigating intermittent high tail latency for streaming responses in us-west-2. We have mitigations in place; some customer requests may see longer token latency. We'll update in <1h>."
eli: good. David — please add kernel upgrade job id and responsible deploy pipeline owner to the RCA doc.
david: added: kube-job id `upgrade-2026-03-15-0304`, owner `infra-images`. also dumping `kubectl describe node` for affected nodes to artifacts.
carla: quick hypothesis refinement: not just scheduler policy — perf shows increased `irq_time` and `softirq` handling which can be caused by a kernel interrupt handling reg change. I'm pulling changelog now.
frank: changelog shows commit referencing `nohz_full` and scheduler latency improvements in 5.19.1 — plausible cause.
ops-bot: reminder — please attach ALL logs to incident folder before closing.
eli: decision: roll back nodepool to previous AMI in 10 node batches. infra to run smoke after each batch. if rollback reduces p95 to baseline, we mark kernel change as root cause and open postmortem.
ben: infra has approved emergency rollback. starting batch-1 rollback (nodes 1–10).
carla: continuing perf samples on remaining nodes. I'll post artifacts per batch.
frank: monitoring metrics dashboard. current p95 is trending down from 1.1s -> 420ms cluster-wide after initial canary & scaling.
alice: customer advisory sent to support distribution list. will post external update if SLA impacted customers require notice.
eli: great coordination. next steps for RCA doc: collect traces, perf counters, `dmesg` outputs, kernel changelog, k8s job ids, and sequence of node upgrades. assign owners in doc.
frank: taking next oncall — I'll keep the channel updated every 15m. handing over to me now. eli will stay as incident lead for RCA write-up.
eli: handoff acknowledged. thanks team. final note: initial root cause hypothesis = kernel scheduler/interrupt handling changes in 5.19.1 causing increased scheduling latency under our workload. will confirm in RCA with full artifacts.
ops-bot: Incident status changed to "mitigated" (p95 reduced to baseline). Please do post-incident review within 72 hours.
